useWhen: The user points at a folder of loose materials and asks for an inventory, an overview or a plan to organise it.
The user asks what is in a collection of downloaded, scanned or collected files and how it could be arranged.
nearMiss: Moving, renaming, copying or deleting the materials.
Summarising the content of one document in depth.
Reading a single attached file that belongs to no selected folder.
Sorting a mailbox or chat history rather than files.
Extracting tabular data into a spreadsheet.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.description: The folder to inventory: a path, or a folder the conversation identifies without contradiction.

inputs.name: organising-principle
inputs.description: The user's intended arrangement, for example by topic, date, source, project or status.

inputs.name: include-or-exclude
inputs.description: File types or subfolders to include or exclude from the inventory.

inputs.name: output-location
inputs.description: Where the new index file is written. Without it, the index is returned in the conversation.

read: The selected folder's one-level directory listing.
The contents of the materials inside that folder, as far as they are readable.
write: One new index file at a user-chosen location.
The conversation itself, when the user does not want a file.

outputs.name: materials index
outputs.description: A Markdown index with a summary, one row per material carrying its classification and the evidence used, a not-classified list with reasons, and a proposed naming and sorting plan explicitly marked as not applied.

successEvidence: Every file in the folder appears exactly once, either classified or listed as not classified with a reason.
Each classification cites the material content it used rather than the file name alone.
The summary counts match the listing that was actually read.
The proposed plan is labelled as not applied and applying it is described as a separate user action.
The index states that no material was moved, renamed, rewritten or deleted.

failureBehaviour.behaviour: Ask which folder to inventory and produce no index for a guessed folder.
Report the exact path and why it cannot be used, then stop. Do not substitute a parent or sibling folder.
Say which capability is missing. With listing only, deliver a name-only index clearly labelled as such; with nothing readable, stop. Never present a guess as a classification.
Report how far the listing got, mark the index partial and list the materials that were not reached.
Write a new index with a distinct name, state what changed since the previous index, and leave the earlier index and every material untouched.
